newsitem.title: IRAN: Tajik government, opposition hold talks in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government, opposition hold talks in Iran.

text.p: A U.N. envoy and officials from Tajikistan's government and opposition met in Tehran on Tuesday to prepare for peace talks in Moscow, Tehran radio said.

It said Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Mahmoud Vaezi, the U.N. special envoy to Tajikistan, Gered Merrem, and Tajikistan government and opposition officials met to prepare for renewed peace talks to be held in Moscow.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri are due to attend the Moscow talks, the radio said, without giving a date for the meeting.

The Tehran meeting was also attended by ambassadors of Russia, Pakistan, and unspecified Central Asian states along with Afghanistan's envoy to Iran, who is loyal to the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, the radio added.

Merrem is trying to rescue a shaky United Nations-sponsored ceasefire in Tajikistan which was reconfirmed at peace talks in July. The ceasefire was first signed in September 1994 but both sides have continued to accuse each other of violations and fighting has broken out in areas east of the capital Dushanbe.
Iran has also tried to mediate in the conflict and hosted talks between Rakhmonov and Nuri in Tehran last year.

The Tajik rebels are loyal to Islamic opposition leaders driven into exile in Afghanistan and Iran after losing a clan-based civil war which broke out soon after the independence from the Soviet Union.
